prompt: Some people believe that private cars should be banned from the centres of large cities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Bans are rarely the interesting part of a transport policy, and treating this as a question about cars obscures what is actually being decided. A city centre is a fixed quantity of land. Every decision about vehicles is a decision about how that land is divided, and the private car is simply the most expensive user of it per person moved.

Seen that way the case is straightforward. A lane of traffic and the parking that serves it consume a strip of the most valuable ground in the country in order to move a few hundred people an hour; the same strip carries many times that number as a bus lane, a cycle track or a pavement. Nothing in that arithmetic depends on disliking motorists. It is why districts that reallocate the space almost always end up busier than before, and why the retailers who campaign hardest against pedestrianisation are so often the ones who benefit from it.

The objection that matters is not about congestion or trade but about who gets left behind. For a wheelchair user, a plumber with a van, or a cleaner finishing a shift at two in the morning, a car is not a lifestyle choice, and a ban presented as a moral correction of selfish behaviour will fall hardest on people whose behaviour was never the problem. Any scheme worth supporting begins with blue badges, loading windows and a night bus that actually runs.

Sequence matters just as much. Restrict driving before the alternatives exist and the policy fails on its own terms, generating a resentment that outlives the administration which introduced it. Build the tram first and the traffic thins before anyone has been compelled to do anything.

So I agree, with the emphasis moved. The aim is not to punish drivers but to stop allocating the scarcest public land to the least efficient possible use of it — and done in that order, the ban is less a prohibition than a formality confirming a change most people have already made.
title: Banning cars from city centres
